title: A completion file's value may name where it is defined and what replaces it, an attachment may depend on another argument and may ask for a check, a list may be completed a segment at a time, and a parameter typed as a union of string literals completes its members
scope:
Six additions to the completion files of [0242](0242.md): a value's source location, read by hover and go-to-definition; an
attachment that applies only when another argument has a given value; a list of values completed one segment at a
time; an opt-in check of the string literals at a parameter; a replacement for a deprecated value, offered as a quick
fix; and completion of a parameter whose declared type is a union of string literal types, which the compiler
derives without a file. Whether `nvs check` reports the opt-in check is left to a later record.
dependsOnText:
[0242](0242.md) (the completion file, its loaded table and the guarantee that an item changes only the string the
cursor is in), [0240](0240.md) (a string argument mapped to its parameter through `crate::arguments`, which also
finds the argument a `when` names).

summary.headline: Completion values can show their source, depend on an argument and be checked
summary.body:
A value in a completion file can name the file and line that define it. Hover shows its description, and
ctrl+click opens that line. A list can depend on another argument, so a translation method offers only the keys of
the domain you passed. Long keys such as `shop.cart.title` complete one part at a time. The editor can warn about a
string not in the list. A deprecated value can name its replacement, and the editor offers to change it. A
parameter typed as fixed strings, such as `'paid'|'shipped'`, completes them without a file.
